sources.capture_note: Same evidence capture already in the Atlas (evidence aae3591c-c0ab-58ae-87e0-0de19995dcdf, status source of SI3); title, publisher, family, licence, publication date, retrieval time and hash are copied unchanged so the builder resolves to that one evidence record. Re-captured on 23 October 2026 with the fragment capture script (local_data/country-research-jp-kanto-p2/scsk-itpnavi-2026-10-datacenter.html, 85,423 bytes): byte-identical, sha256 9f09b855...7172c, so the page has not changed since 15 October. www.scsk.jp robots.txt (HTTP 200) was read and recorded before the first request and allows /sp/ and /news/.
sources.summary: SCSK's IT Platform Navigator report of 1 October 2026 on a site visit to its netXDC Inzai campus in Inzai, Chiba. It states that SCSK has provided data-centre services since 1988 under the netXDC brand, mainly in Kanto and Kansai; that the visit was to Chiba No.3 Center (SI3); and that the campus has three data centres, SI1 to SI3, of which SI3 (service start May 2022) is the newest. It then describes campus-level operating measures at the netXDC Inzai campus: silencers and noise barriers on generators and other outdoor plant with measured compliance with Noise Regulation Act limits, and temperature measurements confirming that the campus does not discharge waste heat that materially raises surrounding air temperatures. It gives no capacity, occupancy or IT load for SI1 or SI2.
sources.date_semantics: JSON-LD datePublished 2026-10-01T09:00:00+09:00. 1 October 2026 is the dated operator report describing the campus and its three data centres in the present tense. It is not the site-visit date (unstated), an opening date or a construction milestone; SI1 opened in 2002 and SI2 in 2015 according to the campus specification page.

sources.title: SCSK netXDC Inzai campus specifications
sources.capture_note: Same evidence capture already in the Atlas (evidence d0ca01f5-86a3-50df-a249-31815b643aa7, identity context of SI3); metadata copied unchanged so the builder resolves to that one evidence record. Re-captured on 23 October 2026 (local_data/country-research-jp-kanto-p2/scsk-netxdc-inzai-campus.html, 34,064 bytes): byte-identical, sha256 52c73ac6...4c24.
sources.summary: SCSK's undated netXDC Inzai campus (印西キャンパス（SI）) page. Its specification table lists three buildings on the campus: Chiba Center (SI1), opened 2002, 14,353 m2 gross floor area, eight storeys plus penthouse with four server-room floors equivalent to 1,200 racks, SRC base-isolated, gas-turbine generators with 72 hours of fuel-free running; Chiba No.2 Center (SI2), opened 2015, 15,586 m2, six storeys with four server-room floors equivalent to 1,600 racks, steel base-isolated with vertical damping, gas-turbine generators; and Chiba No.3 Center (SI3), opened 2022, 12,919 m2. All three have extra-high-voltage main/standby supply. The rack figures are facility specifications, not occupancy or measured IT load.
sources.date_semantics: Undated facility specification page; used for building identity and opening years only. No status observation is taken from it.

sources.title: SCSK: 連結子会社への会社分割（簡易吸収分割）に関するお知らせ (transfer of the data-centre system-operations business to SCSK System Management)
sources.capture_note: Captured 23 October 2026 (170,238 bytes, 2 pages); read with pdftotext. Found through Impress Cloud Watch's report (cloud.watch.impress.co.jp/docs/news/2119564.html). Names of company officers and the contact person in the notice are not copied.
sources.summary: SCSK's notice of 23 June 2026 that, with effect planned for 1 October 2026, it transfers by simple absorption-type split the system-operation business of its Data Center Division's service-infrastructure department (described in section 4 as data-centre operation business; sales of JPY 891 million in the year ended March 2026) to its wholly owned subsidiary SCSK System Management. The notice states that SCSK's name, head office, representative, business description, capital and fiscal year are unchanged; it does not mention the netXDC buildings or brand. SCSK's 1 October 2026 report still presents the netXDC Inzai campus as SCSK's own.
sources.date_semantics: Dated 23 June 2026. Context for the operator role only; no status observation is taken from it.

Linked from the council's planned-agenda page for the committee (jp-kanto-p2-koto-council-agenda-page), which carries 更新日 9 October 2026. www.city.koto.lg.jp robots.txt (HTTP 200) was read and recorded before the first request and allows both paths.
sources.summary: Agenda of Koto City Council's Disaster Prevention and Urban Development Special Committee for 16 October 2026. Among items carried over for continued deliberation it lists petitions specifically about the planned data-centre construction in Sengoku 3-chome: 7陳情第13号 (the Sengoku 3-chome data-centre construction plan), 7陳情第43号 (its effect on the planned Sengoku new station), 8陳情第08号 (the plan from a local disaster-prevention viewpoint), 8陳情第09号 (asking the council to resolve for withdrawal of the data-centre construction plan being planned in Sengoku 3-chome), 8陳情第11号 (verification of living-environment and disaster aspects of the large data-centre plan) and 8陳情第15号 (third-party verification of the large data-centre construction), plus general data-centre petitions. It records that the plan is still before the committee in October 2026; it does not state the plan's stage, consent or works.
sources.date_semantics: Agenda posted by 9 October 2026 (page 更新日) for the 16 October 2026 meeting. Used as the in-window government record that names the Sengoku 3-chome data-centre construction plan as a current plan (announced). It is not a permit, a building confirmation or a construction observation, and the petitions themselves are third-party submissions recorded by the council.

sources.capture_note: Captured 23 October 2026 (409,959 bytes, 3 pages); read with pdftotext and page 1 rendered with pdftoppm at 300 dpi. The document names no private individual.
sources.summary: The ward building-coordination section's reference for the committee's 25 June 2026 deliberation of the petition on the Sengoku 3-chome data-centre construction plan. Plan outline: 江東区千石3丁目2番 (remaining lot numbers undecided), site area 9,478.42 m2, building area 6,310 m2, gross floor area 22,640 m2, height 51.4 m, steel frame, five storeys above ground, planned construction period July 2026 to March 2029. A location map outlines the 計画地 in the south-west of the block north of Sendaibori River Park, with two site photographs and the operator's renderings. Timeline: the ward's large-data-centre early-notification guideline took effect on 1 February 2026, when the operator put up its notice sign; the sign notification was received on 5 February and seven briefings were held from 6 February; on 7 May 2026 the operator put up the Tokyo dispute-prevention-ordinance sign and on 30 May it held the ordinance briefing. The operator's explanations cover roof-level outdoor units, low-noise plant, emergency generators and twelve 100,000-litre underground A-heavy-oil tanks. The operator is not named.
sources.date_semantics: Dated 令和8年6月25日 (PDF created 11 June 2026). Identity, project description and locator source; its 25 June date is outside the admission window and is not used as the status observation. The construction period is a plan, not a stage.
